title: The thing of most worth is bringing souls to Christ
setting: John Whitmer was 26 and living at his father’s farm in Fayette, New York. Joseph Smith was there in June 1829 finishing the Book of Mormon translation. John sometimes wrote as scribe when Oliver Cowdery was away. He was probably baptized that month, and he asked Joseph to inquire about his duty. This revelation answered him, and an identical one went to his brother Peter Jr.
summary: The revelation addresses John by name and speaks as Jesus Christ, his Lord and Redeemer. It says the Lord speaks with sharpness and power. It says it will tell John something only he and the Lord know. John has many times wanted to know what would be of most worth to him. The revelation blesses him for that desire and for speaking the Lord’s words. It then answers: the thing of most worth is to declare repentance. By doing so he may bring souls to Christ and rest with them in the Father’s kingdom.

contextNote.title: A private question, a plain answer
contextNote.text: Verse 4 reveals John’s private question: what would be “of the most worth” to him? Verse 3 frames the answer as personal, something known only to John and the Lord. Verse 6 then answers in one line: declare repentance and bring souls to Christ. The reward named is not wealth or status but rest with those souls. So the worth John sought is measured in people, not in his own gain. In this passage, “worth” means what lasts into the Father’s kingdom.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 12–17 notes that John and Peter Whitmer Jr. received the same answer to a sincere personal question. Verse 4 says John had asked “many times”; what does verse 6 suggest you might ask the Lord about your own priorities?
reviewNote: Read all 6 verses. Official heading gives Fayette, June 1829, to John Whitmer, and refers to the heading of section 14. JSP historical introduction read for John’s age, scribal work, likely June baptism, and the order of his and Peter’s revelations. Text is nearly identical to section 16.
